about: One script for both of a replica's syncs: the browser's FenecSync (web/fenec.js, run by web/fenec.sync.scenarios.test.js) and the native core every binding drives (crates/fenec-abi/src/sync, run by crates/fenec-abi/tests/scenarios.rs).

A scenario starts with no replica and plays its steps in order. `do` says what happens: start, restart (the app opened again over the replica it kept), seed / change (a stream event of the shape at index `shape`, 0 by default), drop (every stream ends), fire (every timer asked for runs out), answer (the oldest write request not yet answered gets `status`, `seq` as Fenec-Seq and `body`; status 0 is no answer at all), write (an app's write: insert / update / delete / batch), net (whether the server is reached: a stream or GET /collections made while it is not fails at once), stream_status (the next stream opened is answered with it), online (the platform's network signal), token (a new token handed over), schema (what GET /collections answers from now on).

After each step the runner checks `expect`: requests (the GETs and POSTs made during the step: method, path, auth, key = the Idempotency-Key, body = the lines sent, lines = how many), streams (each stream opened: its path and query, auth), rows (the replica's rows of a collection by id, each row's named fields), pending (writes not yet answered), refused (the statuses refused writes were told with), token_asked, waits (each timer asked for, [min, max] ms), ready (every shape seeded), error (a start or a write refused before anything is sent).

An object expected is a subset of the one that came; a list is whole. A string `<name>` is any value, the same wherever the name comes again and another than every other name's: a key made for an insert, an Idempotency-Key. In a step's data a bound `<name>` stands for its value, so the server's copy of a row carries the key the app made. `@name` in rows or puts is a fixture.

Writes are written with their fields in alphabetical order, as the builders render them in the order given: JavaScript keeps an object's order and the native runner's JSON sorts it. A temporary id is 2^52 = 4503599627370496 and up.

Where the platforms differ on purpose a scenario says why in `differs`, and a step's expect_js / expect_native hold each side's own. Both runners write the names that passed to target/sync-scenarios/, and integrations/sync-scenarios-check.mjs fails unless both ran every one.

scenarios.name: the seed fills the replica with the shape
scenarios.covers: sync.html#start, mobile.html#sync: the schema from the server, the rows from the seed

scenarios.name: a shape's filter and projection go in the stream's query string
scenarios.covers: sync.html#shapes: ?field=op.value, select with id always added

scenarios.name: a shape's operators read as the REST surface's
scenarios.covers: sync.html#shapes: not, in, is null

scenarios.name: two shapes over one collection are refused
scenarios.covers: sync.html#shapes: one collection per shape

scenarios.name: a start with no shape is refused

expect.error: at least one shape is required

scenarios.name: a shape names its collection
a shape's operator must be one it knows
a shape's in takes a list with something in it
two shapes over two collections are ready once both are seeded
changes land, and a row leaving the shape goes
scenarios.covers: sync.html#stream: state, not operations; a row that no longer matches arrives as a deletion

scenarios.name: a change before the seed is not applied
scenarios.covers: an incremental diff over an unseeded copy would leave the changed rows alone

scenarios.name: a dropped connection resumes from its cursor, a change sent again harmless
scenarios.covers: sync.html#horizon: since=<cursor>, backoff 250 ms with 30% jitter

scenarios.name: a stream that cannot reconnect backs off, doubling to 15 s
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync: 250 ms doubling to 15 s; an open stream starts the count again

scenarios.name: the server out of reach at the first start: its collections are asked for again
scenarios.covers: a replica with no collection yet waits for the server's schema, and backs off meanwhile

scenarios.name: an optimistic insert shows at once and is matched by its key
scenarios.covers: sync.html#optimistic: a temporary id from 2^52, a key made for it, the server's copy taking its place

scenarios.name: an insert keeps the key it was given
several documents are one write, each with its own temporary id

body.query: put tasks [{status: $1, title: $2, key: $3}, {status: $4, title: $5, key: $6}]

scenarios.name: an insert into a shape with no key waits for the server's copy
scenarios.covers: sync.html#optimistic: with nothing to match it by, the server's copy would leave two

scenarios.name: an insert naming its id shows at once, and is put back when refused
scenarios.covers: the server's copy is matched by the id the write names

scenarios.name: an update shows at once, is sent, and its echo changes nothing
scenarios.covers: sync.html#optimistic: update and delete work by the filter, needing no key

scenarios.name: a delete shows at once, is sent, and its echo changes nothing
an update that reaches no row is still sent
scenarios.covers: the replica may not hold a row the server does

scenarios.name: an increment made offline is sent as the expression, and the server's sum is the one kept
scenarios.covers: sync.html#optimistic: inc() runs on the replica at once and on the server again, so two replicas' offline increments both land; this is either of the two, the other's landing first

scenarios.name: writes go one at a time, in order, each under a key of its own
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync: a write that lands after one written after it would leave the server holding the earlier

scenarios.name: an insert outside the shape leaves no temporary row once the stream passes it
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync: the server answered at seq n; a stream past n holds the server's copy, or the shape does not

scenarios.name: an answer the stream already passed lets the temporary row go at once
an update of an unanswered insert reaches the server's copy by its key
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync, formerly a browser bug: the temporary id is the replica's alone

scenarios.name: a delete of an unanswered insert reaches the server's copy by its key
an update of an answered insert not yet echoed reaches it by its key too
a batch is one write, sent as one /batch and refused whole
scenarios.covers: sync.html#batches: one request, one key, put back whole the last first

scenarios.name: a batch that lands is matched as its writes would be
a 409 refuses an insert: put back, and told
scenarios.covers: sync.html#optimistic, mobile.html#sync: a unique value held

scenarios.name: a 403 refuses an update: the row put back as it was
scenarios.covers: a token's rules

scenarios.name: every other 4xx refuses, and the writes behind it go on
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync: only 401, 408 and 429 of the 4xx are not refusals

scenarios.name: a 5xx keeps the write and sends it again under the same key
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync, formerly a browser bug: a server error is not a refusal

scenarios.name: a 408 and a 429 are answers to come back, not refusals
no answer at all keeps the write, and the same key lands it once
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync, formerly a browser bug: a network failure is not a refusal; Idempotency-Key makes the second send the first's answer

scenarios.name: a send that keeps failing backs off to 15 s, and a refusal after it still puts back
a 401 asks for a token, and the write goes again with it
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync: a tokenProvider asked on a 401, setToken

scenarios.name: a 401 on the stream asks for a token, and the stream opens with it
a stream refused with a 5xx is tried again with backoff
offline, writes wait, and go first when the network is back
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync: setOnline; writes left are sent before the streams open, so what they bring holds them

scenarios.name: back online, the backoff is forgotten
a write while the stream is down is sent all the same
a restart keeps its pending writes, their keys and its cursor
scenarios.covers: mobile.html#sync and sync.html#persist: an app closed with writes unsent sends them when it opens again, in order, each once

scenarios.name: after a restart a write the server cannot take now lets the streams open
a write refused after a restart is put back from what was kept
a restart makes its temporary ids after the ones it kept
a restart with another shape is seeded afresh
scenarios.covers: the cursor is the shape's: another filter holds other rows

scenarios.name: past the horizon the server seeds again, and an unanswered insert's row stays
scenarios.covers: sync.html#horizon, mobile.html#sync, formerly a browser difference: a seed writes over and keeps the rows of writes not yet answered

scenarios.name: a seed keeps an answered insert's row while the seed is from before the answer
a seed's copy of a pending insert takes its place
a schema change on the server: the replica takes the new schema and the whole shape
scenarios.covers: the server owns the schema (sync.html#schema); a change says schema: true, and the collection is made again from GET /collections

scenarios.name: a field renamed on the server is read from the new seed
rows with a field the replica has not got are taken for a schema change
scenarios.covers: a seed past the horizon after an alter says nothing of the schema; its rows do

scenarios.name: rows a @ttl lets go of arrive as deletes, and read as gone before
scenarios.covers: the server's sweep deletes expired rows; the replica's @ttl leaves them out of a read at once
